exposure: COVID-19 pandemic period (pre-pandemic, first pandemic wave, second pandemic wave)
outcome: Composite maternal adverse outcomes (emergency caesarean section, obstetric anal sphincter injury, hysterectomy, sepsis, anaesthetic complications, prolonged hospital stay)
Composite perinatal adverse outcomes (stillbirth, neonatal death, preterm birth, brain injury, small for gestational age, prolonged hospital stay)
cohort: The cohort consisted of women giving birth and babies born in the National Health Service in England between April 1, 2018, and March 31, 2021.
finding: Existing ethnic inequalities in adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes were sustained, not tempered, during the COVID-19 pandemic, despite substantial changes to maternity services and care.
mod_finding: The overall incidence of maternal adverse outcomes, which included emergency caesarean section, initially decreased in the first pandemic wave but then increased in the second pandemic wave.
